environment: Python 3.14.7, Node v24.19.0, shell shims for gh and glab on PATH (no network), scratch git repos, S-013 code from commit e575c1b as the reference for VS-9

cases.title: 44 odd glab bodies keep the result shape
cases.given: a gitlab repo and a glab shim that prints each body: array, string, number, bool, null, 100000 nested arrays, regex as number, list, object, invalid RE2, NUL, control chars, lone surrogate, 1 MB regex, NaN, BOM, two documents, empty output, 8 MB body, 2M-entry array
cases.when: read_rules(repo, [feat/a, feat/b]) runs for each body
cases.then: each result has the five top keys; every rule has exactly the five spec keys with the right types; a non-string regex gives no rule; a string regex gives one rule; unparseable output gives one note and unchecked true
cases.expected: each result has the five top keys; every rule has exactly the five spec keys with the right types; a non-string regex gives no rule; a string regex gives one rule; unparseable output gives one note and unchecked true
cases.actual: 44 of 44 cases match. No exception. Probe: a regex of only spaces gives a rule (not covered by the spec).

evidence.title: examples run
evidence.inline: VS-7 examples: 44 cases, probes: whitespace-only regex: rules=[{"source":"gitlab","kind":"regex","pattern":"   ","negate":false,"label":"push rule"}] unchecked=false

cases.title: Property: 1500 random glab bodies against a model written from the spec
cases.given: a seeded generator of JSON bodies (null, {}, odd regex types, invalid regexes, extra keys, bad text) and sample lists
cases.when: read_rules runs through a glab shim for each body
cases.then: one regex rule exactly when branch_name_regex is a non-empty string; no rule and no note for other parsed values; one note and unchecked for unparseable text
cases.expected: one regex rule exactly when branch_name_regex is a non-empty string; no rule and no note for other parsed values; one note and unchecked for unparseable text

evidence.title: glab body property
evidence.inline: property glab body: seed=14001 runs=1500 violations=0

cases.title: Property: gitlab_rule is total and matches the model for 2000 values
cases.given: the pure function gitlab_rule and 2000 generated values
cases.then: returns the one regex rule for a non-empty string regex in a dict, else None; never raises
cases.expected: returns the one regex rule for a non-empty string regex in a dict, else None; never raises

cases.title: Probe: failure notes for odd stderr
cases.given: glab exits 1 with stderr: boom, empty, multi-line, 200000 characters, control characters, NUL, CR LF, U+2028
cases.then: one note starting rules unknown on gitlab:, empty rules and by_sample, unchecked true, no exception
cases.expected: one note starting rules unknown on gitlab:, empty rules and by_sample, unchecked true, no exception
cases.actual: All 10 give that shape. The note keeps line breaks and NUL from stderr in 3 cases, and a 200000 character stderr gives a 200025 character note. The spec states no limit, so these go to seeds.

cases.title: Exit codes 1, 2, 127 and 255 with a JSON error body on stdout; exit 0 with the same body
cases.given: a glab shim that prints {"message": "404 Project Not Found"}
cases.when: read_rules runs for each exit code
cases.then: non-zero exit gives the rules unknown note and unchecked true; exit 0 gives no rule, no note and unchecked false (ADR f2c2)
cases.expected: non-zero exit gives the rules unknown note and unchecked true; exit 0 gives no rule, no note and unchecked false (ADR f2c2)

cases.title: One glab call with the literal argv and the repo as cwd, for hostile sample names
cases.given: samples --help, -x, $(touch pwn), a b, empty, newline, unicode, 50000 characters, ../../etc
cases.then: one call; argv is api projects/:fullpath/push_rule; cwd is the repo; no sample reaches argv; by_sample has one key per distinct sample; no file pwn
cases.expected: one call; argv is api projects/:fullpath/push_rule; cwd is the repo; no sample reaches argv; by_sample has one key per distinct sample; no file pwn

cases.title: S-013 GitHub cases give the same results before and after the refactor
cases.given: the S-013 version of branches.py (commit e575c1b) and the S-014 version, one gh shim; two operators, negate true and false, a skipped non-pattern rule, a failure on the second sample, a failure with empty stderr, a JSON object, non-JSON output, no samples
cases.actual: 7 of 7 scenarios equal; rules, by_sample, notes and unchecked as before

cases.title: Property: 1200 random gh scenarios give equal results on the S-013 and S-014 code
cases.given: a seeded generator of gh outputs: rule lists, other rule types, junk entries, exit codes, bad JSON, 0 to 4 samples, up to 4 steps
cases.when: read_rules runs on both versions through the same shim
cases.then: equal results; for well-formed rules, exactly the five keys, a kind among the four values, a string pattern
cases.expected: equal results; for well-formed rules, exactly the five keys, a kind among the four values, a string pattern
cases.actual: 0 differences in 1200 runs; no shape violation for well-formed rules. 177 runs with malformed gh rules (no parameters) give kind null and pattern null in both versions (seed).

cases.title: Determinism and input immutability
cases.given: a glab shim that prints a regex body
cases.when: read_rules runs twice with the same samples list
cases.then: equal results; the samples list is unchanged
cases.expected: equal results; the samples list is unchanged
cases.actual: matches. Probe: by_sample lists and the rule dicts are shared between samples and rules (spec states no immutability, so a seed).

seeds.title: gh rule with missing parameters returns kind null and pattern null
seeds.detail: A gh body entry {"type": "branch_name_pattern"} with no parameters gives a rule with kind null and pattern null, in the S-013 code and the S-014 code alike. R-026 acceptance says kind is one of four values and pattern is a string. GitHub always sends the parameters, so no real input shows it. Fix: drop the rule or give a note when operator or pattern is not valid (github_rule).

seeds.title: A forge failure note keeps line breaks, NUL and any length of stderr
seeds.detail: With stderr 'a\nb' the note is 'rules unknown on gitlab: a\nb'. A 200000 character stderr gives a 200025 character note. NUL and CR pass through. The spec says only that the note holds <stderr>. The plan's VS-5 asks for one line and a bound. Fix: collapse whitespace and cut to a fixed length in _run_forge_cli.

seeds.title: A regex of only spaces becomes a rule
seeds.detail: {"branch_name_regex": "   "} gives one regex rule with pattern '   '. The spec treats an empty regex as no rule and says nothing about spaces. GitLab would likely reject such a push rule.

seeds.title: read_rules results share list and dict objects
seeds.detail: For a gitlab push rule, every by_sample entry is the same list object, and its rule dict is the same object as the one in rules. A caller that edits one entry changes all of them. The spec states no immutability rule. Fix: copy the list and the rule per sample.
